samples.summary: New `DateCell` component (preference-driven text + `title` tooltip) has no test at all
samples.evidence: `DateCell` is the whole point of the feature in the list: it calls `useDateFormat()`, renders `formatListDate(value, format)` and sets `title={formatFullDateTime(value)}` (document-list.tsx:240-247). The added tests only cover the pure helpers (tests/app/documents/document-list-utils.test.ts) and the store (tests/lib/date-format-preference.test.ts). Nothing renders `DateCell` or `dateColumn`'s cell, so the acceptance criterion "both columns carry a `title` tooltip with the full localized date+time in every format" is unverified — swapping the two formatters, dropping `title=`, or passing the wrong value would leave the suite green. The frontend also has no `tsc` lane, so a wrong prop wouldn't be caught elsewhere either. Searched: tests/app/documents/ contains only document-list-utils.test.ts and tab-name.test.ts; grep for `DateCell`/`document-list` across packages/frontend returns no test file.

samples.summary: Settings `Select` — the only UI that writes the preference — is untested
samples.evidence: The new Dates section wires `value={dateFormat}` / `onValueChange={(v) => setDateFormat(v as DateDisplayFormat)}` (settings/page.tsx:69-84). There is no test file for the settings page anywhere (no packages/frontend/tests/app/settings/, and grep for `settings/page` finds only src references), so a mis-wired handler, a missing option, or a control that never reflects the stored value would ship green. The store's own tests call `setDateFormat` directly and therefore cannot catch this.

samples.summary: Acceptance criterion "sorting is independent of the display format" is asserted only in a comment, never in a test
samples.evidence: `dateColumn`'s doc comment and `formatListDate`'s comment both claim sorting always compares raw values via `compareDates`, but no test exercises the column's `sortingFn` (or asserts ordering is unchanged under `exact`). Existing `compareDates` unit tests in tests/app/documents/document-list-utils.test.ts cover the comparator in isolation, not its use by the column, so a future cell/accessor change that made ordering format-dependent would not be caught. Searched tests/app/documents/* and grepped for `sortingFn` in tests.

samples.summary: Current-year assertion is locale-fragile and only weakly pinned
samples.evidence: `expect(formatted).not.toMatch(/2026/)` alone would also pass for the em-dash fallback or an empty string; only the companion `toMatch(/25/)` keeps it honest, and neither asserts the month is present. A stronger assertion (e.g. the full expected `Intl.DateTimeFormat` output for a fixed locale) would fail loudly if the options object regressed to day-only.

finding.summary: New `DateCell` component (preference-driven text + `title` tooltip) has no test at all
finding.evidence: `DateCell` is the whole point of the feature in the list: it calls `useDateFormat()`, renders `formatListDate(value, format)` and sets `title={formatFullDateTime(value)}` (document-list.tsx:240-247). The added tests only cover the pure helpers (tests/app/documents/document-list-utils.test.ts) and the store (tests/lib/date-format-preference.test.ts). Nothing renders `DateCell` or `dateColumn`'s cell, so the acceptance criterion "both columns carry a `title` tooltip with the full localized date+time in every format" is unverified — swapping the two formatters, dropping `title=`, or passing the wrong value would leave the suite green. The frontend also has no `tsc` lane, so a wrong prop wouldn't be caught elsewhere either. Searched: tests/app/documents/ contains only document-list-utils.test.ts and tab-name.test.ts; grep for `DateCell`/`document-list` across packages/frontend returns no test file.

verdict.reason: The new `DateCell` component exists exactly as described (document-list.tsx:240-247: `useDateFormat()`, text via `formatListDate(value, format)`, tooltip via `title={formatFullDateTime(value)}`) and is used for both date columns (document-list.tsx:269 via `dateColumn`). No test in the repository renders it: a repo-wide grep for `DateCell` returns only the source file, the task doc, and prior review artifacts; no test file imports `document-list.tsx` or `DocumentList` (only src/app/documents/page.tsx:6 and workspaces/workspace-documents.tsx:7 do). I also searched beyond the paths the reviewer tried — colocated `src/**/*.test.tsx` suites including `src/app/documents/__tests__/**`, the whole `tests/**` tree, any `e2e/**` directory, and `playwright.config.*` (none exists) — so there is no browser/e2e lane covering it either. The two added suites stop at the seams: document-list-utils.test.ts tests only the pure formatters, and date-format-preference.test.ts tests the store/hook via `renderHook`. Hence the composition — which formatter feeds the visible text vs. the `title`, and that `title` is set at all — is unasserted; swapping the formatters or dropping `title=` would keep the suite green. The task's own acceptance criterion (docs/tasks/active/20260812-date-display-format-todo.md:26) explicitly requires the tooltip on both columns, and its test plan (lines 53-56) covers only the helpers/store. That is a clear behavior change with no meaningful test, i.e. major under this lens.

finding.summary: `useDateFormat`/`subscribe` — the mechanism that makes the preference reactive — has no test at all
finding.evidence: tests/lib/date-format-preference.test.ts only exercises the plain functions `getDateFormat`/`setDateFormat`. The only "notification" test (lines 35-44) attaches its own raw `window.addEventListener("wafflebase-date-format-change", ...)` and counts dispatches; it never calls `subscribe()` or renders `useDateFormat`. If `subscribe` were a no-op, registered the wrong event, or failed to unsubscribe on cleanup, or if the `getServerSnapshot` argument were wrong, every test in the suite would still pass. The headline behavior of the change (Settings choice instantly updating the documents list, and cross-tab sync via the `storage` event) is therefore entirely uncovered — the `storage` listener at line 79 has no test whatsoever. Frontend already has React component/hook tests (e.g. tests/components/notifications/use-mark-read.test.tsx), so this is testable here.

verdict.reason: The finding claims useDateFormat/subscribe has "no test at all" and that the storage listener is untested, but the cited test file contains a dedicated describe("useDateFormat") block (lines 119-203) that renders the hook with renderHook and exercises precisely those mechanisms. Lines 131-141 assert a same-tab setDateFormat("exact") re-renders the hook from "relative" to "exact" (would fail if subscribe were a no-op or listened on the wrong event). Lines 143-157 dispatch a real StorageEvent("storage") and assert the hook updates, directly covering the window.addEventListener("storage", onChange) at src line 79. Lines 177-202 spy on add/removeEventListener and assert both listener types are registered and then removed with the same handler reference on unmount, covering the cleanup path. Lines 125-129 and 159-175 additionally cover the mount snapshot and the memory-mirror path through the hook. None of these are vacuous or over-mocked: the real module functions are invoked and assertions are on hook output that only changes if the subscription actually works. The tests do run: vite.config.ts:267-269 sets environment "jsdom" with include "tests/**/*.test.ts" (matching this file) and setupFiles tests/setup.ts, and @testing-library/react is a declared devDependency (package.json:83) with test script "vitest --run" (package.json:15). The reviewer's quoted evidence that the file "only exercises the plain functions getDateFormat/setDateFormat" and "never calls subscribe() or renders useDateFormat" does not match the working tree.

finding.summary: New `readStoredTheme`/`writeStoredTheme` localStorage guards ship with no test
finding.evidence: The diff changes theme-provider behavior from "throws (blanking every route) when localStorage access throws" to "falls back to default / silently drops persistence". Grepping tests/ for `theme-provider`/`ThemeProvider` returns no files, and only tests/lib/date-format-preference.test.ts and tests/components/text-formatting/font-recents.test.ts mention localStorage at all. Nothing can fail if the try/catch guards are removed or if the fallback returns the wrong value (e.g. `null` vs `defaultTheme`), while the analogous guards in date-format-preference.ts did get read/write-throw tests.

verdict.reason: A dedicated test file for exactly these guards exists and runs. packages/frontend/tests/components/theme-provider.test.tsx renders the real ThemeProvider (imported from "@/components/theme-provider", not mocked) under a describe block "ThemeProvider storage guards": it mocks Storage.prototype.getItem to throw and asserts the provider does not throw on mount and falls back to "system" (defaultTheme, not null) — the exact null-vs-defaultTheme case the finding says nothing can catch; it mocks setItem to throw and asserts the chosen theme still applies for the session (state + documentElement class); and it covers happy-path persistence to "vite-ui-theme" and restore-on-mount. The file is inside the vitest include globs (packages/frontend/vite.config.ts:268 includes "tests/**/*.test.tsx"), so it is executed. The finding's core claim — grepping tests for theme-provider/ThemeProvider returns no files — does not reproduce against the working tree.
